signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Fed Hawkish Repricing
signals.text: USD/NOK trades at 9.553, extending well above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 9.361) in a confirmed short-term momentum surge. The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard registers a critical bilateral divergence, with USD outperforming peers by +2.099% (n=9) while NOK drops -1.977% (n=2), generating a massive 4.075% spread. Multiple Fed officials, including Collins and Daly, explicitly flagged the need for additional tightening, pushing US 10Y yields up to 5.149% and sending the 2Y yield differential to -17bp, moving 16bp in favor of the USD over the past 5 sessions. While retail positioning shows an extreme 91% long stance that historically warrants contrarian caution, the macro rates impulse dominates near-term price action. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK, sustained upside momentum backed by hawkish Fed repricing. Catalyst: Fed Governor Jefferson Speech at 00:00 UTC. Risk: Sharp pullback in US Treasury yields below 5.00% invalidating the rates-driven dollar impulse.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium vs Options Put Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.74, holding firmly above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 158.13) as price action consolidates just below key intervention thresholds. A massive +266bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.89% vs TONA 1.23%) continues to anchor structural demand for the pair while broad market stress remains contained with VIX at 19.1. However, institutional options markets display acute defensive positioning: 1M 25d Risk Reversals print at -1.79, indicating significant bid for JPY calls and USD puts to hedge downside tail risks. Positioning data reveals a JPY COT LF net short of -21,213 contracts (pctl 92, z +1.46), confirming the speculative carry trade is heavily crowded in the upper decile of its 52-week range. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY, structurally supported by rate differentials while below key threshold levels. Catalyst: Next BoJ policy meeting on 18 Dec. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 triggering direct MoF foreign exchange intervention.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Hawkish Fed Repricing + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1025, entrenched below its SMA20/50/200 cluster with the 20-day SMA at 1.1185, confirming a clear downtrend. Fed policy rate at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% maintains a +135bp nominal carry advantage for the dollar, reinforced by an OIS SOFR vs €STR spread of +145bp. CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds net short EUR at -104,030 contracts (pctl 2, z -1.80), reflecting stretched institutional short positioning at the bottom decile of its annual range. Conversely, retail sentiment stands at an extreme 87% long, creating a stark institutional-versus-retail positioning divergence where retail is attempt-fading the institutional downtrend. Realized volatility runs at 5.5% against 1M ATM IV of 6.2%, reflecting a mild 0.7% vol risk premium as options markets price steady downside pressure. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, downside momentum backed by rate spreads and institutional order flow. Catalyst: Next ECB policy meeting on 17 Dec. Risk: Short covering rally if US macroeconomic data turns sharply softer.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Technical Downtrend vs Positive Carry Premium
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6777, breaking lower and trading entirely below its SMA20/50/200 cluster with SMA20 at 0.6972, leaving price extended by 3.43 ATRs from its 20-day average. The pair maintains a positive AUD carry advantage, with RBA policy rate at 4.85% vs Fed at 4.00% generating an 85bp rate spread (and -96bp OIS carry favoring AUD). Economic sentiment shows persistent divergence, as Australia's Economic Surprise Index sits at -6.1 against the USD ESI of +11.2, underscoring broader macroeconomic headwinds for the Aussie dollar. 1M 25d Risk Reversals show a moderate put skew of -1.30 alongside IV at 7.8% vs HV30 at 8.0%, pricing moderate hedging demand for further downside extensions despite the carry buffer. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, technical downtrend overriding positive carry backdrop. Catalyst: Next RBA policy meeting on 8 Dec. Risk: Surge in global commodity prices triggering a broad repricing in growth-sensitive currencies.
